text: Is GSE309890 the same thing as GDS309890?

Abstract
This report addresses whether the GEO accession “GSE309890” is identical to “GDS309890.” Using the GEO accession-resolution tool, we queried both identifiers and retrieved their full accession metadata. Two distinct records were returned: GSE309890 (Series) with UID 200309890 and GDS309890 (curated GEO DataSet) with UID 309890. Each has a unique FTP directory and GEO landing page, demonstrating that they are separate entries rather than aliases. Thus, GSE309890 ≠ GDS309890; they refer to different record types in GEO.

I. Introduction
Background. The Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) stores several record types: Series (GSE) capture an experiment’s overall design and all its samples; DataSets (GDS) are NCBI-curated, secondary interpretations of selected Series. Users often confuse whether a GDS accession is simply another label for the underlying GSE.
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.
Knowledge Gap. Whether the Series accession GSE309890 is effectively the same object as GDS309890 was uncertain.
Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: Determine if GSE309890 and GDS309890 point to the same GEO record. Hypothesis: The two accessions encode distinct records because GSE and GDS prefixes denote different GEO object classes.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. We resolved each accession via the GEO resolver to examine UID, entry type, and storage paths.
Materials. GEO: accessed through geo_resolve_accession.
Procedures.
1. geo_resolve_accession(accessions="GSE309890 GDS309890").
Statistical Analysis. We compared returned fields (uid, entry_type, ftp_directory_url) for identity; equality of any single field would suggest duplication.

III. Results
Data Presentation.
Table 1. Comparison of returned metadata.

| Query       | UID       | Entry type | FTP directory (root)                                   |
|-------------|-----------|-----------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| GSE309890   | 200309890 | GSE       | …/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/                     |
| GDS309890   | 309890    | GDS       | …/geo/datasets/GDS309nnn/GDS309890/                   |

Findings. The two accessions resolve to different UIDs, belong to different GEO object classes (Series vs DataSet), and reside in separate FTP hierarchies.

IV. Discussion
Interpretation. Distinct UIDs and record classes confirm GSE309890 and GDS309890 are not interchangeable; GDS309890 is a curated subset or reinterpretation of data, whereas GSE309890 is the original submitter-provided Series.
Context. GEO designates GSE for primary studies and GDS for curated datasets, matching the observed distinction.
Limitations. The resolver does not reveal how much the GDS re-uses or filters the GSE content; further inspection of record details would be required.
Conclusion & Future Directions. GSE309890 and GDS309890 are separate GEO records. Future work could examine sample overlap and processing differences between them.

References
[1] GEO resolver result for GSE309890: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890  
[2] GEO resolver result for GDS309890: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GDS309890  

Acknowledgments
We acknowledge NCBI GEO for providing publicly accessible gene-expression records and the GEO resolver service for accession mapping.
